Consumer complaint narrative:
On XX/XX/2020, I noticed that I had lost my credit card. I immediately reported it lost and requested a new credit card from Bank of America. I received e-mail notification that a new card would be mailed to me. I did not receive one, and Bank of America did not put a freeze on the account. 

On XX/XX/2020, after the XXXX holiday, I logged into my Bank of America account online. There were in store charges in excess of {$3000.00} made during the holiday week on the card. I promptly called to report the fraud, to understand why the account had not been frozen, and why I had never received a new card in the mail. They were very apologetic, froze the account, and issued a new credit card number. They also opened a fraud dispute and temporarily credited my account. 

After 30 days, I received a notice saying that my fraud claim was denied because I had made purchases at these vendors in the past. However, that is not true. Whoever had my card spent ~ {$2000.00} at XXXX XXXX, which I had not been to in recent memory. In addition, {$600.00} at XXXX, and my phone provider was XXXX at the time. I explained the facts again, and the fraud agent opened an appeal case. 

After 30 additional days, I received a second notice that the claim was denied for the same reason. I called once more, and explained the facts. I did not have the card in my possession, as I had reported it lost prior to any of these in store purchases. The fraud agent then instructed me to file a police report, which I had not been instructed to do until this time. 

I then filed a local police report, and submitted it to the fraud department. Some time later, I received yet another notice that the claim was denied for the same reason as the first two times. 

Ultimately, I ended up paying for the fraudulent charges because it would be too expensive to hire legal counsel. It is aggravating that a very reputable financial institution would handle a fraud claim in this manner. I have since transitioned my core banking to a local credit union, and will soon close all accounts held with Bank of America because of how this claim was handled two years ago. I was recently made aware that I could file a complaint with the CFPB so that at least my experience would be on the record.
